subject: platform claims the task gates rest on
scenario: Both task gates rest on one platform behaviour: exit 2 blocks. If a future Claude Code drops TaskCreated or TaskCompleted from its blocking set, nothing errors -- the hooks keep running, their stderr goes nowhere anyone acts on, and two gates silently stop being gates while every document still says they hold. This case tries to make that silent change loud. Failure looks like: the capability record is not marked load_bearing, or the drift checker does not read the binary for it.
expected_behaviors: hook.TaskCreated.can_block is recorded as available, load_bearing, and names the script that depends on it.
The absence of dependency edges in the payload is still recorded, because it is the reason the task graph is this plugin's own artifact rather than a mirror of Claude Code's list.
check_platform_drift.py reads the installed binary for both the payload shape and the blocking set.
The capability model names the version it was verified against.
failure_conditions: A gate depends on exit 2 blocking and nothing checks that it still does.
The payload claim is taken from the published documentation rather than the binary. On 2026-08-24 the two disagreed on six points.
Dependency edges appear in the payload and the graph keeps inferring what the platform is now willing to state.

checks.description: The model names the version it was checked against, so drift is visible.

notes: Verified 2026-08-28 against 2.1.250 by reading the binary: TaskCreated sends task_id, task_subject, task_description?, teammate_name? and a deprecated team_name; it sits in the same blocking set as Stop, TeammateIdle and TaskCompleted; and its blocking path deletes the created task and strips its id from every other task's edges.
